The Oloyan of Oyan, Oba Adekeye Oluyeye, has appealed to the Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, over the alleged non-payment of salaries of traditional rulers and chiefs for seven months. The monarch, speaking in Yoruba, made the appeal in a video posted on Facebook by Osogbo Updates on Wednesday. “The king is starving. They are starving the king and chiefs,” he said. Oluyeye said the affected traditional rulers in Odo Otin were many, putting the number at 17 kings and 440 chiefs. “In this Odo Otin, there are 17 kings. The chiefs alone are 440,” he said. It is frustrating. Isn’t it?” he said. Oluyeye said President Bola Tinubu had played his part, saying: “The President has done what is proper.” Ooni, Olubadan, others meet in Ibadan Adeleke: Osun’s $26.56m debt rise not from new loans NUJ honours CNN award-winning journalist Afolabi He asked that his message be passed on to the governor. “Please tell Ademola, hunger is killing the king. He is really starving the king,” he said. PUNCH Online reports that the Nigeria Labour Congress directed workers in Osun State to embark on a three-day sympathy strike on Sunday over the continued withholding of local government statutory allocations.
